clue.text: Where philosophers are trained?

parts.note: Surface reading: a college or academy where students of philosophy learn their trade.; Setter's reading: a doctrine or outlook shared by a group of thinkers, which the question mark flags as a pun on an educational establishment.

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark warns that the 'school' is not a building: the phrase means a shared set of ideas, such as Stoicism, that philosophers follow.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a body of doctrine held by followers of one thinker, jokingly pictured as an academy with classrooms.

clue.text: Original sin can act without a gut feeling

indicators.note: original means novel, newly made, so the letters of sin are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of sin are the anagram fodder
a can is a tin

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter is removed

parts.note: the word act supplies its letters minus one

explanation.surface: Original sin made us act without a gut feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Original sin' looks like the theological phrase, but 'Original' signals INS; then TIN and CT, which is ACT 'without' A.
explanation.definitionFit: An instinct is an innate impulse or intuition, a feeling in the gut.

clue.text: Coach tour has altered boarding time

indicators.note: boarding means getting on, so the letter goes inside the rearranged word
has altered means changed, so the letters of tour are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of tour are the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A coach tour has changed its departure time.
explanation.walkthrough: Coach suggests a bus, but it is the definition, a teacher. 'altered' gives TUOR, with T boarding after TU.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor is a private teacher, one who coaches a student.

clue.text: Old-fashioned to plant herb without style

indicators.note: to plant something is to set it in the ground, so one piece is sunk inside another
'without' in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: sage is a kitchen herb
tone is manner or style, as in the tone of a letter

explanation.surface: A gardener dismissing the planting of herbs without flair as dated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here means outside, not lacking: the herb goes round the style rather than losing it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stone Age is the prehistoric era, so calling a thing stone-age says it is hopelessly out of date.

clue.text: Unsalted crab is late addition to snacks

indicators.note: a salt is a sailor, an AB, so unsalted means the sailor is removed

parts.note: the word crab supplies its letters minus the sailor
a PS, postscript, is a late addition to a letter

explanation.surface: A cook adds unsalted crab to the snacks at the last moment.
explanation.walkthrough: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor, and 'salt' is slang for a sailor, so 'Unsalted' removes AB from CRAB. Crisps are what Americans call potato chips.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain crisps are thin fried potato slices sold in packets, a common snack.

clue.text: Pretend I am angry with one suspect

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: something suspect is dodgy or not right, so the letters are out of order

parts.note: fodder taken as printed, eight letters

explanation.surface: Someone feigning fury at a suspect under questioning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretend' reads as a verb but is the adjective, as in a pretend friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretend as an adjective describes something made-up or existing only in the mind, a child's word for fictional.

clue.text: Attempt to elevate iron building

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word makes it read from bottom to top

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a fort is a fortified building

explanation.surface: Workers trying to hoist the ironwork of a building into place.
explanation.walkthrough: Fe, from the Latin ferrum, is worth knowing as iron; in a down answer, 'to elevate' turns it upward.
explanation.definitionFit: An effort is a try at doing something, so both nouns name an endeavour that may or may not succeed.

clue.text: Twist of her logic treated as support for smokers

indicators.note: a twist bends things out of their straight course, so the letters are turned about
treated means processed or worked on, so the letters are changed

parts.note: fodder: fifteen letters, 'treated' included

explanation.surface: Someone's twisted reasoning being taken as backing for people who smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treated' works twice here: it is both part of the fodder and a hint that the letters are processed. 'Support' is the physical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A cigarette holder is a slim tube that grips a cigarette, literally propping it up for the person puffing on it.

clue.text: Lead and gold material that will transmit electricity

parts.note: to lead is to conduct, as with a tour
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A chemistry fact: lead and gold both carry an electric current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' reads as the metal, which fits the surface, but it is the verb, pronounced to rhyme with 'need'.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics a conductor is any substance, like copper, through which current flows readily.

clue.text: Mother trimmed outfit worn by soldier on leave

definitions.note: describes the clothes, a noun phrase, rather than naming them

indicators.note: trimmed means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: mother is mum
the word splits as out and fit: out signals rearranging fit

explanation.surface: Mum trimmed an outfit for her son, a soldier home on leave.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram is hidden in one word: 'outfit' is out (signal) plus FIT, giving FTI. Shortened MUM gives MU.
explanation.definitionFit: Mufti is civilian dress worn by service personnel off duty.

clue.text: Worried our town appears behind the times

indicators.note: to worry something is to shake or tear at it, so the letters are disturbed

parts.note: fodder, seven letters

explanation.surface: A resident fretting that the home town looks dated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worried' reads as anxious, the surface sense, but the setter means shaken about, as a dog worries a bone.
explanation.definitionFit: Outworn means out of date or obsolete, no longer suited to present-day ways.

clue.text: Evidence links nothing to artist at Italian address

indicators.note: to link things is to join them in a chain, so pieces sit side by side

parts.note: a sign is evidence or an indication
nothing is zero, the letter O
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: An investigation where evidence ties nobody to a painter's Italian home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' is not a street and number but a form of address, a title used when speaking to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Signora is the Italian title for a married woman, equivalent to Mrs or madam when speaking to her.

clue.text: Get tasteless book scrapped

indicators.note: something scrapped is thrown away, so a letter is discarded

parts.note: bland food lacks flavour
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A demand that a vulgar book be pulped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tasteless' suggests vulgar, as the surface wants, but it means lacking flavour; 'Get' is the definition, in the sense of securing something.
explanation.definitionFit: To land something, such as a job or a contract, is to secure or obtain it.

clue.text: Notes a time to move flat

indicators.note: moving things shifts their positions, so the letters change places

parts.note: fodder, ten letters

explanation.surface: A reminder that it's time to relocate from one's apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like an adjective or a musical term beside 'Notes', but it is the British noun for an apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: A maisonette is a British two-storey apartment, a kind of self-contained dwelling within a larger building.

clue.text: Con man misrepresented Freud's art

indicators.note: misrepresenting gives a false version, so the letters appear in a wrong order

parts.note: fodder, nine letters, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A swindler passing off fakes of paintings by Lucian Freud.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'Freud's' is ignored, as punctuation always is in crossword fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A con man is a swindler who tricks people out of money, just the kind of cheat this answer names.

clue.text: To be liberal with butter at first appears healthy

indicators.note: 'at first' puts one piece at the front, ahead of the other

parts.note: butter is a fat
to be free with something is to be liberal with it

explanation.surface: The irony of spreading butter generously and calling it healthy eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter' names an example of fat rather than a synonym, which is why it goes first on the setter's instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Food with no fat in it is marketed as good for the body, so the label signals wholesome eating.

clue.text: Transport by rail perhaps, if time

indicators.note: perhaps signals a possible version of the word, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Goods might go by rail, if there's time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges RAIL to AIRL, followed by IF and T.
explanation.definitionFit: An airlift is the carrying of supplies or people by aircraft, often in an emergency.

clue.text: Assign place to a student

indicators.note: 'to' means added on, so one set of letters is attached to the others

parts.note: used as it stands
L is a learner driver, the crossword student
to place is to locate, to put in position

explanation.surface: A school office giving a new pupil a place.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface places the student in a school, but the pieces go A, L, then the verb, with 'to' putting 'place' last.
explanation.definitionFit: To allocate is to distribute or give out a share, so both verbs mean handing something to someone.

clue.text: Brave of one to get books about rising depression

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
NT is the New Testament, a set of books
re means about or concerning

indicators.note: in a down clue, something rising reads from the bottom upward

parts.note: a dip is a hollow in the ground

explanation.surface: Praising someone for reading self-help books about low mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' suggests low spirits, but it is a physical dip in the ground, and 'about' is a piece rather than a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrepid describes a fearless person who faces danger undaunted, which is what courage means.

clue.text: Good to respect expert

parts.note: to honour someone is to respect them
an able person is skilled, expert

explanation.surface: Advice that it pays to defer to a specialist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expert' looks like a noun for a specialist, but it is the adjective meaning skilled.
explanation.definitionFit: An honourable person is principled and upright, so the word describes moral goodness.

clue.text: Irritate with unnecessary loss of two points

indicators.note: a loss means something is taken away, so letters are removed

parts.note: needless means not required
S for south, a compass point, twice

explanation.surface: A sports fan annoyed by a team carelessly dropping two points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Points' suggests a score, but in crosswords they are compass points, here S and S.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to provoke or goad them with persistent small jibes until they are annoyed.

clue.text: Everyone united regarding appeal

parts.note: all means everyone
U is the abbreviation for united, as in football club names
re means regarding or concerning

explanation.surface: A public campaign where everybody backs the same plea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appeal' reads as a request, but it means attractiveness.
explanation.definitionFit: Allure is attractiveness or charm, the power to draw people in, just as appeal can mean.

clue.text: Make an impression and so on at hospital

indicators.note: 'at' places one thing next to another, so the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: etc, et cetera, means and so on
H is the map symbol for a hospital

explanation.surface: A new doctor trying to impress colleagues on the wards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make an impression' suggests impressing people, but it is literal: cutting a design into a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to engrave lines into metal or glass with acid or a tool, literally marking the surface.

clue.text: Silly of Anne to get involved with one

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: getting involved means getting mixed up, so the letters are jumbled together

parts.note: fodder as printed

explanation.surface: A disapproving remark that it was foolish of Anne to start a relationship with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is gossip about Anne's love life, but 'involved' just means mixed up, and 'one' adds a letter to the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means senseless or foolish, lacking any sensible content, the same as daft.

clue.text: Circle missing outlines with cooking implement

indicators.note: cooking the books means falsifying them, so the letters are doctored
something missing is absent, so a letter must be taken out

parts.note: O is a circle by its shape
'outlines' without its O

explanation.surface: A kitchen tool for drawing a round shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooking implement' reads as one phrase, but 'cooking' is the anagram signal and 'implement' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A utensil is a tool or piece of equipment, especially one used in the kitchen.

clue.text: Set dance disrupted by English student

indicators.note: a thing disrupted has something breaking into it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: the conga is a line dance
E is the abbreviation for English
L is a learner driver, the crossword student

explanation.surface: A formal set dance interrupted by an English pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set dance' looks like one phrase for a formal dance; 'Set' is split off as the verb meaning to harden.
explanation.definitionFit: To congeal is to thicken from liquid to solid, which is what jelly or gravy does when it sets.

clue.text: Five tucked into healthy share

indicators.note: tucking a thing into another puts it inside

parts.note: hale means healthy, as in hale and hearty
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: Five people tucking into a wholesome meal they will divide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucked into' suggests eating, but here it means inserted.
explanation.definitionFit: To halve something is to divide it into two equal portions, a way of splitting it between people.

clue.text: Can well recall engineers being doubtful at cut

definitions.note: a phrase describing what a good memory does, defining an adjective

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers

indicators.note: cut means having something removed, here the letters of at

parts.note: doubtful means tentative

explanation.surface: Engineers in doubt at a cut ask who can remember the plan well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can well recall' looks like a verb phrase, but it describes a memory that holds on, which suits an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A retentive memory is one that holds on to information, able to remember things.
